lessons.title: In the clothes shop
lessons.goal: Ask for clothes in a shop, try them on and say if they fit.

tip.title: Ça me va: talking about fit
tip.body: French uses aller (to go) for 'fit' and 'suit': Ça me va (it fits / suits me), Ce pull te va bien (that jumper suits you). Clothes size is la taille — Je fais du 40, said du quarante; shoe size is la pointure. Object pronouns go before the verb: Je peux l'essayer ? (l' = it). Essayer is é-sé-YÉ: the final -er sounds like é.

lessons.title: Colours and what to wear
lessons.goal: Describe clothes and colours and decide what to wear.

tip.title: Colours agree — mostly
tip.body: Colours come after the noun and agree like other adjectives: un pull vert, une robe verte, des chaussures vertes. Blanc becomes blanche. Colours named after things — marron, orange — never change: des chaussures marron. Two-word colours don't change either: une cravate bleu marine. Listen for the ending: in vert the t is silent, in verte you hear it.

lessons.title: Sales and paying
lessons.goal: Ask about reductions, pay and take your receipt.

tip.title: Prices and percentages
tip.body: A sign saying -30 % is read moins trente pour cent. In prices the comma is the decimal point: 49,90 € is quarante-neuf euros quatre-vingt-dix. Watch the liaison: deux‿euros, trois‿euros, vingt‿euros (you hear z or t). The receipt is le ticket (de caisse) — keep it if you might exchange something. C'est pour offrir ? means 'Is it a gift?': many shops will wrap it for you.

lessons.title: Plus cher que… and ce, cet, cette, ces
lessons.goal: Compare clothes and point at them with ce, cet, cette, ces.

tip.title: Comparing and pointing
tip.body: Compare with plus … que (more), moins … que (less) and aussi … que (as): Cette veste est plus chère que l'autre. The adjective still agrees. Superlative: le / la / les plus … — le manteau le plus chaud du magasin ('in the shop' is du magasin). Bon → meilleur (better), le meilleur (the best); never say plus bon. Demonstratives: ce pull, cet anorak (masculine before a vowel or mute h), cette robe, ces chaussures. Cet and cette sound the same.

culture.title: Les soldes and magasiner
culture.body: In France, les soldes are regulated: there are two official sale periods a year, in winter (from January) and in summer (from late June), with dates fixed by the state. Shops cut prices in stages — la deuxième démarque, la troisième démarque — so waiting can pay off, but your size may be gone. In Québec, to go shopping is magasiner (On va magasiner samedi ?), a jumper or T-shirt is often un chandail, and socks are des bas, while in France they are des chaussettes.
